newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 30.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Jan. 30

WASHINGTON - America Online, the country's largest computer online service, agreed to give refunds or credits to nearly all of its 8 million subscribers as compensation for weeks of problems in connecting to the overloaded service.

MEXICO CITY - As drug interdiction in the Caribbean has increased and Mexico has curtailed incoming flights by huge cargo planes stuffed with cocaine, traffickers have turned to the virtually unpatrolled eastern Pacific Ocean as their primary route for sending the drug to the United States.

WASHINGTON - As the federal government hands more of its research to private contractors and science is run increasingly as a business, a growing number of laboratories are saving money by hiring scientist-temps.

WASHINGTON - The White House provided its most detailed explanation yet of how the president came to host a coffee attended by Democratic party fund-raisers, the leaders of 17 major financial institutions and the nation's top banking regulator.

WASHINGTON - The Archdiocese of Washington will spend $1 million on 14 Catholic elementary schools in the District and improve services for at-risk and Latino students to try to stem a more than 20 percent drop in enrollment in the last decade.

WASHINGTON - The Republicans' advertisement at the height of the partisan debate over balancing the budget in late 1995 dubbed it the "Million Dollar Medicare Challenge," but now it is turning into a million-dollar legal headache.
